f.title: Treat lack of efficacy, misuse, overdose, medication errors and occupational exposure as adverse reactions
f.statement: For these guidelines an adverse drug reaction is a noxious and unintended response to a medicinal product, including lack of efficacy, occurring at any dosage and arising from use within or outside the terms of the marketing authorisation (including overdose, off-label use, misuse, abuse and medication errors) or from occupational exposure. Adverse drug reaction, adverse reaction and adverse event are used interchangeably.
f.clause: ii. Definitions

rows.quote: “Adverse Drug Reaction / Adverse Reaction” means a response to a medicinal product which is noxious and unintended including lack of efficacy and which occurs at any dosage and can arise from: ~ a) Theuse of product within the terms of the marketing authorisation b) The use of product outside the terms of the marketing authorisation, including overdose, off-label use, misuse, abuse and medication errors; c) Occupational exposure. In this document, adverse drug reaction, adverse reaction and adverse event will be used interchangeably.
rows.location: ii. Definitions
rows.review_note: Review: definition kept because it widens what counts as a reportable adverse reaction. Double-check: definitions are not phrased as a duty; level Recommended per guide.

f.statement: The agreement or contract between the MAH and the local QPPV shall state that the local QPPV: (1) acts as the single point of contact for the Authority on pharmacovigilance and product safety; (2) establishes and maintains a system so that suspected ADRs reported to MAH personnel, including medical representatives, are collected, collated, processed, evaluated and submitted within the timelines in the guidelines; (3) serves as point of contact and is available during pharmacovigilance inspections; and (4) provides input on regulatory documents relating to product safety.

rows.quote: 1. The local QPPV shall act as a single point of contact for the Authority on all matters relating to pharmacovigilance and safety of a product granted Marketing Authorisation. 2. The local QPPV shall establish and maintain a system which ensures that information about all suspected adverse drug reactions/events which are reported to the personnel of the MAH, including medical representatives, is collected, collated, processed and evaluated and submitted to the Authority in line with the timelines stipulated in the Guidelines. 3. The local QPPV shall serve as a point of contact and be available during pharmacovigilance inspections. 4. The local QPPV shall provide input on regulatory documents relating to the safety of a product granted Marketing Authorisation.
